uncited: It is distinguished from sibling methods by focusing on the raw memory layout and buffer management infrastructure rather than the rendering algorithm itself ([GSPull](2773-gspull.md)), error-based densification ([Composite Error Map and Densification/Pruning Scoring](3396-composite-error-map-and-densification-pruning-scoring.md)), or specific network architectures ([GS-W Network Architecture](5927-gs-w-network-architecture.md)).
The family operates on a Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) paradigm, where each attribute type is stored in a separate contiguous linear buffer [5568-splat-data-buffer-layout.md].
Spherical Harmonics coefficients are stored as $N \times D \times 3$ floats, with indexing $idx = ((i \times D) + d) \times 3 + c$ [5570-spherical-harmonics-coefficient-layout.md].
Dynamic scene management supports incremental `append` operations and dynamic buffer resizing [6907-dynamic-gaussian-splatting-scene-management.md].
When writing to buffers, linear values are converted to log-space via $\log()$.
During load, validate header bounds: refuse if non-finite, negative size, or failing to enclose the root's world AABB.
Each node/instance record is exactly 128 bytes.
Data is organized into bounded, non-overlapping sections.
